svg.aria-label: Diagram: the Microsoft Customer Agreement billing hierarchy of billing account, billing profile and invoice section, showing what each scope owns, that the billing profile is a pricing boundary because tiered prices are computed per profile, and that the invoice section is the delegation boundary where subscription creation is granted
svg.title: What each billing scope actually owns, and the two boundaries that cost money
svg.text: Three scopes above the subscription, and only one of them is really about paperwork
A Microsoft Customer Agreement billing account. Each level owns different things, and two of them change what you pay and who can build.
billing account
The agreement
Sold-to details, and the country/region and currency that everything below inherits and cannot change.
At sign-up only the person who signed up has access here. Owner or contributor can create billing profiles.
Roles granted at this level inherit onto every profile and section below, and cannot be removed lower down.
Grant here only for people who genuinely need the whole estate.
∟ billing profile
One invoice
One monthly invoice, generated at the start of the month. Payment methods, PO number, bill-to address.
Azure plans are enabled here. Purchase policies for reservations and Marketplace are applied here.
Usage is aggregated per profile, so tiered prices are worked out per profile and never across them.
A pricing boundary. Adding one here changes the bill.
∟ invoice section
One heading on it
A grouping of costs on that invoice. Every profile has one by default; subscriptions attach here.
The Azure subscription creator role exists only at this scope, and nowhere else.
Section owner or contributor can move a subscription between sections of the same profile.
A delegation boundary. This is where vending is granted.
Splitting the invoice splits the price tier
Microsoft's own worked example. 100 TB of block blob storage billed to one profile costs 180.5 — 50 TB at 1.84 per TB,
then 50 TB at the next-tier 1.77. Split 50/50 across two profiles and both halves are charged the first-tier 1.84, so the
same usage costs 184.0. That is 1.94% more, for an org-chart decision nobody costed.
And a shared-scope reservation does not cross that line either
Reservations with shared scope apply to subscriptions in a single billing profile and are not shared across profiles. A
second invoice created for neatness can quietly stop a discount reaching half the estate.
